claim: The equivalence of Laplace-isospectrality and representation-equivalence for hyperbolic orbifolds is KNOWN to hold in dimension 2 (Doyle-Rossetti) but was an open question in dimension 3, which this 2024 paper partially addresses by constructing hyperbolic 3-orbifolds that are i-isospectral for all i yet not representation-equivalent.
stance_target: state of knowledge on isospectrality-vs-representation-equivalence for hyperbolic orbifolds by dimension
quoted_support: The converse, whether Ω∙-isospectrality of two hyperbolic 3-orbifolds implies representation equivalence of the corresponding groups, has until now been an open question... The converse does hold for hyperbolic 2-orbifolds [22] and it has been conjectured to hold in dimension 3, too.

claim: This 2024 paper produces a pair of closed connected orientable arithmetic hyperbolic 3-orbifolds of volume 0.251... that are i-isospectral for all i but not representation-equivalent, possibly the smallest known such pair.
stance_target: smallest known isospectral hyperbolic 3-orbifold examples as of 2024
quoted_support: Theorem A. There exists a pair of closed connected orientable arithmetic hyperbolic 3-orbifolds with volume 0.251... that are i-isospectral for all i, but not representation equivalent, only one of which has a cyclic isotropy group of order 10.

claim: The paper's methods are number-theoretic (regulators, torsion homology, Galois representations) applied to dimension-3 hyperbolic orbifolds, and it contains no discussion of triangle orbifolds, cone-surface heat trace, or heat-coefficient counting for 2-dimensional cone orbifolds -- confirmed by direct full-text search of the 65-page PDF.
stance_target: this paper being a competing finite-coefficient determinacy result for hyperbolic cone orbisurfaces
